propositions: Code review's v3 impact model discards verifiers' prod_impact and trigger_likelihood judgments for maint-lane tests findings, preventing findings on load-bearing paths (prod=medium/high) from reaching blocking thresholds despite high consequence.
A contract-contradiction antipattern (e.g., contract declares 'stale>0 allowed' while co-shipped test asserts 'stale=0') is not currently detected, allowing contradictory artifacts to ship together.

The v3 maint-lane dampener (×0.5 when churn90 absent, affecting 80% of findings) artificially compresses test-finding scores to ~0.30, below the advisory@0.95 threshold, despite the binary's legitimate high impact.

V4 redesign must restore prod_impact/trigger_likelihood consumption, add the forbids_contract_allowed_state binary with tightening guards, lane-split the severity scaling (serious undamped; moderate prod_impact-keyed; debt churn-amplified-only), and restrict reversibility floor to consequence lanes to prevent unintended debt-binary escalation.

Replay on 1881 code-v3 sidecars shows v3 blocks 42/1243 changes (3.4%); v4 with tests@0.54 blocks 99/1243 (8.0%, operator-accepted), with zero demotions and hand-verified true-positive rate >96% in the new set.

Tests blocking threshold must shift from 0.95 to 0.54 post-v4 to capture moderate-maint and serious-maint findings now properly scaled, while keeping internal-edge findings (prod=none/low) advisory at ~0.27–0.30.
